name: Ellenbarrie Industrial Gases Ltd
title: Ellenbarrie Industrial Gases Ltd - 544421 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

read.thesis: Core gases segment margin rose to 39% from 38% and on-site plant commissioned, but merchant plants slipped a year to H2 FY28 and consolidated margin fell to 36% on freight and EPC mix.

summary.headline: Q2 FY27 revenue rose 28% YoY to ₹1,143 mn, but consolidated EBITDA margin fell to ~36% from 39% on freight and employee costs.
summary.overview: Revenue from operations was ₹1,143 mn, up 28% YoY and 16% QoQ, with H1 FY27 revenue at ₹2,130 mn (+23%). Consolidated EBITDA rose to ₹407 mn from ₹387 mn in Q1, but margin slipped to ~36% from ~39%, which management attributed to diesel-linked transport costs, longer-distance deliveries and employee costs (including increment arrears and project engineering build-out). Core gases segment margin improved to ~39% from 38%. The 325 TPD Durgapur on-site plant was commissioned in September 2026, and a ₹480 crore BHEL EPC contract for a 1,200 TPD air separation unit in Odisha was won, with commissioning expected in FY29.

financial_highlights.change: up from ₹387 mn in Q1 FY27

financial_highlights.metric: Gases related products and services revenue growth

financial_highlights.change: broadly similar in Q1 and Q2

segments.name: Gases (core on-site and merchant)
segments.commentary: Revenue up ~27% YoY in Q2 with segment margin ~39%, up from 38% in Q1; argon contribution rose to ~16% of mix, split roughly half volume and half price.

segments.name: Project engineering
segments.commentary: Newly won ₹480 crore BHEL EPC contract (1,200 TPD ASU, Odisha) over eight quarters, with Q1 of execution being Q3 FY27; management guided to a segment margin of high single digits to low double digits.

guidance_outlook: Long-term revenue growth guidance of ~20% for the core gases business; management expects ~20% annualised growth in the near term, driven by spare capacity at Uluberia 2 and the new Durgapur on-site plant.
Freight and power-related margin pressure expected to normalise over the next couple of quarters, with a 2-3 month lag between cost increases and customer pass-through.
Long-term gases segment margin target of ~40%, which management says the business is close to at 39%.
Durgapur on-site plant gives a full quarter of revenue in Q3 FY27; on-site revenue expected to lift margins in H2.
Two merchant plants in north and central India expected to contribute from H2 FY28 (about mid-year), after delays from state land allotment and statutory approvals.
Capex of ~₹450 crore for FY27 and FY28 remains on track; management indicated peak revenue potential of ~₹450-500 crore to ~₹800 crore across assets at full utilisation, with timing uncertain.
capex_capacity: Durgapur, West Bengal: 325 TPD on-site plant commissioned September 2026 under a 15-year take-or-pay on-site gas supply agreement; total on-site capacity now above 1,000 TPD.
Uluberia 2 merchant plant commissioned in Q4 FY26 and still has spare capacity to be utilised; management did not give plant-wise utilisation.
Two merchant plants (north and central India) delayed by about a year to H2 FY28, attributed to state land allotment and statutory approvals; ramp-up assumed at 6-8 quarters.
BHEL 1,200 TPD cryogenic ASU in Odisha: EPC over ~8 quarters (about 24 months), commissioning in FY29; initial engineering under way.
Planned solar gases facility in central India to add a portfolio of four to five gases; no significant helium or electronic gases plans.
demand_pricing: Pharma is the second most important end market after steel, with customers expanding capacity; healthcare (hospital supply) is stable with consistent growth.
On-site business is almost entirely steel; bulk and merchant customers span a wide range of industries.
Management said some customers' new capex implementation is taking longer than expected.
Argon long-term demand is growing faster than supply; current argon prices are around recent average realisations. Management declined to give quarterly price trends.
Freight costs are linked to diesel and treated as a pass-through; most customers are on long-term contracts that allow cost pass-through.
Coal gasification is seen as a long-term opportunity requiring large oxygen and ASU capacity; company market share is still in single digits.

qa_highlights.question: Will the margin dip be recovered through freight pass-through, price increases, or both?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said long-term contracts allow pass-through of cost increases, with a 2-3 month lag; margins expected to normalise over the coming quarters.

qa_highlights.question: What is the quantum of higher power and transport costs and the expected pass-through?
qa_highlights.answer: Power was about 22% of gases revenue in both Q1 and Q2; management guided that the pass-through percentage would stay near the Q1-Q2 average.

qa_highlights.question: What are the margin and working capital profile of the BHEL EPC contract?
qa_highlights.answer: Margins are expected to be high single digits to low double digits, with working capital as the only capital need; management did not give net margin figures for the project.

qa_highlights.question: Why were the north and central merchant plants delayed from FY27 to H2 FY28?
qa_highlights.answer: Delays came from state land allotment and statutory approvals; management now expects revenue contribution from H2 FY28, around mid-year.

qa_highlights.question: What is the peak revenue potential of the asset base and when could it be reached?
qa_highlights.answer: Current run rate is ~₹400 crore, and full utilisation of new plants adds ~₹300 crore, giving ~₹450-500 crore to ~₹800 crore; timing depends on market conditions and customer ramp-up.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the argon mix increase came from volume versus price?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the ~600 bps increase was roughly half volume and half price, with the new Uluberia capacity adding argon output.

risks_watch: Consolidated EBITDA margin (~36%) is diluted by lower-margin EPC revenue, which will rise as BHEL execution ramps from Q3 FY27 onward.
Diesel and freight cost pass-through lag may keep margins under pressure for another one to two quarters.
Merchant plant timelines have slipped by about a year, and the peak revenue timing (FY29 or FY30) was not committed.
Ramp-up of Durgapur on-site and Uluberia 2 utilisation needs monitoring for the margin uplift management expects.
Capex of ~₹450 crore is being funded from cash and project-level debt; no equity raise is imminent.
Management did not disclose net margin on the BHEL contract or quarterly argon price trends.
summary.management_tone: Confident on the strategic wins (Durgapur on-site, BHEL EPC) and on gas segment margins, but cautious and evasive on timing and quantum: they declined to give BHEL net margins, argon quarterly prices or peak-utilisation timing, and said plant delays were due to government processes.
key_quotes: Ellenbarrie is moving from capacity creation to capacity monetization.
Long term we had indicated that we'll have about 40% margin for the gases segment, which we are very close to at 39%.
These EPC contracts will carry a lower margin than our core gases business, and that's obviously on account of the fact that we are not really employing any long-term capital here.

growth.why: Management guides ~20% annualised core gases growth near term, backed by spare capacity at Uluberia 2, the commissioned 325 TPD Durgapur on-site plant (full-quarter revenue in Q3 FY27), and a ₹480 crore BHEL EPC order; two merchant plants slip to H2 FY28 and the timing of peak revenue is uncertain.
